IFV - FOR (this is a test. If someone has a better idea of where to put these, I'm all ears):
```This repeal's target, GA 703, is certainly verbose, technical, and micromanage-y to a significant degree even by GA standards (kinda predictable considering who wrote it). Its title, "Consular protection [sic] Arrangements," is misleading considering it covers a wide hodgepodge of accommodations members are required to extend to all foreign citizens within their borders, even if said citizens are from a non-member state. These accommodations range from the bizarrely narrow, such as occasionally setting up private meetings between citizens accused of crimes and diplomatic staff, to concerningly broad stuff like facilitating any adoptions permitted under international law and assisting with "repatriations in an emergency if a citizen lacks the means to do so," including shuttling corpses around.

The repeal itself relies on weaker arguments than we'd like. There are numerous boilerplate appeals to national sovereignty where arguments specifically tailored to the provisions in question would be more effective, or where those appeals are unnecessary supplements to otherwise decent arguments. The complaints about the target overreaching are compelling, but the lack of any mention of the nebulous nature of "offer assistance" is odd. We would've also liked to see mention of the obvious loophole in "[t]he assisting state deems itself capable of offering such assistance."

That said, the arguments the repeal does use are still sufficiently convincing. It helps that the target reads like something pumped full of enough helium to lift a small blimp.```
